en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of Immeasurable Life.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great saṃgha of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and great bodhisattvas.
The assembly of bodhisattvas were all seated together in the same gathering.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
He addressed the youth Mañjuśrī: "Mañjuśrī,
above in the direction of the zenith there is a world-system named Immeasurable Mass of Merit."
In that land there is a Buddha named Amitajñānaniścayarāja Tathāgata,
who currently manifests *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and expounds the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
Mañjuśrī, listen attentively.
The people of Jambudvīpa in the southern gate are all short-lived;
their maximum lifespan is one hundred years.
Among them, many die untimely, violent, or by misfortune. Mañjuśrī,
if any sentient beings hear the name of this Tathāgata Amitāyus— his merits, renown,
and essential Dharma— [they shall not suffer such ends].
If one writes it oneself or causes another to write it into a scroll, and then receives, maintains, reads, and recites it in the place where one dwells within one's home,
making offerings with various flower garlands, necklaces, ointments, and powdered incense.
Even if their life span were to come to an end, they would again gain additional years,
fulfilling a full hundred years.
Thus it is, Mañjuśrī.
If there are sentient beings who hear these one hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Life Wisdom Sovereign King,
their longevity will be increased.
If there are sentient beings whose great life is about to end who mindfully recollect the name of this Tathāgata.
One will thereby increase one's lifespan.
Thus it is, Mañjuśrī,
for any son of good family or daughter of good family.
If one desires long life,
there are those who hear the one hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata Amitāyus,
or write them down themselves.
If one causes others to write, receive, uphold, read, and recite [this], they shall obtain such fruits of retribution and be fully endowed with merit.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | āparimitāya | ayuḥkṣayāntāya | supinidarśanāya | rājāya | tathāgatāya | tadyathā | oṃ | sarvasaṃskārāḥ | pariśuddhāḥ | dharmatā | kāyena | svāhā | amoghadharitāya | sarvabhūtaśuddhaye | mahānāya | parivāre svāhā || The World-Honored One further addressed Mañjuśrī:
If one recites these one hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata,
or causes them to be written as a scroll to be received, upheld, read, and recited,
then even if one's lifespan has come to an end, it shall be restored to a full hundred years.
At the end of this life, one shall attain rebirth in the Pure Land of Immeasurable Life, the World of Immeasurable Merit and Wisdom.
The *dhāraṇī* is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | aparimitāya ayu-gaṇanāya supini-siddhaye tathāgatāya | tadyathā | oṃ sarva-saṃskāra-pariśuddhe dharma-te gagane svāhā | amoghadhāri-te svāhā | bhava-viśuddhe mahānaye pari-vare svāhā.* At that time, there were ninety-nine *koṭis* of Buddhas and others.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Points of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the dhāraṇī was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetunā | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharma-tā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Amoghatikāyai | Svabhāva-viśuddhe | Mahānaye | Parivāre | Svāhā.* At that time, there were further one hundred and four *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the *dhāraṇī* was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetunā | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhe | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Mocitakāye | Sarvabhaviśuddhe | Mahānaye | Parivāsa svāhā.* At that time, there were furthermore seventy koṭis of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice, reciting the dhāraṇī of the *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*:

*Namo bhagavate | āryāvalokiteśvarāya | sugatāya | tathāgatāya | tadyathā | oṃ | sarvasaṃskāra | pariśuddhe | dharmate | gagane | svāhā | mocayakari | sarvabhayaviśodhani | mahānaye | parivare svāhā.* At that time, there were further sixty-five *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the *dhāraṇī* was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetunā | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskāra | Pariśuddhe | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Amoghatikāye | Svabhāva-viśuddhe | Mahānaye | Parivare | Svāhā.* At that time, there were furthermore fifty-five *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the *dhāraṇī* was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hṛdayāya | Svapnī-śikhite | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskāra | Pariśuddhe | Dharma-te | Kākanā | Svāhā | Mocaka-te | Sarvabhava-śodhani | Mahānayā | Parivare | Svāhā.* At that time, there were furthermore forty-five *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*.
The *dhāraṇī* is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya ayu-gheyanāya subhānīṣṭāya rājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ sarvasaṃskārā pariśuddhi dharmatā kākanā svāhā | Mucitakāte sarvabhaviśuddhi mahānayā parivare svāhā.* At that time, there were furthermore thirty-six *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Meaning of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the dhāraṇī was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hṛdayāya | Svapnī-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskārā | Pariśuddhe | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Mucitakāye | Sarvabhipratiṣṭhe | Mahānayā | Parivare | Svāhā.* At that time, there were further twenty-five *koṭis* of Buddhas.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Infinite Life*,
and the *dhāraṇī* was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetunā | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskāra | Pariśuddhe | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Amoghatikāye | Sarvārtha-pariśuddhe | Mahānāthe | Parivare | Svāhā.* At that time, there were further Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
At that time, they all spoke with one voice this *Sūtra on the Essential Principles of the Immeasurable Life*,
and the dhāraṇī was as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetunā | Svapnī-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarva-saṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Mocaka-ti | Sarvabhava-śuddhi | Mahānaya | Parivari | Svāhā.* "O son of good family," [he said].
If one writes it out oneself or instructs others to write out this *Sūtra of the Essential Essentials of Amitāyus*,
should their life come to an end, they shall again obtain long life and fulfill their years.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Avalokiteśvarāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe | dharmate | gagane | svāhā | muktikate | sarvabhaviśuddhe | mahānaye | parivare svāhā || If one were to personally transcribe it...
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus* and fully upholds,
recites, and reads it, they shall ultimately not fall into hell.
In every place where one is born, one shall attain the knowledge of past lives (*pūrvajātismṛti-jñāna*).
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāntāya supinīṣṭitārājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | Amoghadhikate sarvabhiprāyaparipūri mahānaye parivare svāhā.* If one should write this out for oneself...
To teach others to transcribe this Sūtra of the Immeasurable Essential Points is equivalent to transcribing all eighty-four thousand scriptures; it is to receive, uphold, read, and recite them.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāya supinidarśanāya rājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ sarvasaṃskāra pariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | Amoghatīkṣṇe sarvabhavaśodhani mahānayapariśrāme svāhā || If one were to write this out oneself...
To teach others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus* is equivalent to transcribing eighty-four thousand copies and erecting stūpas and temples.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Apāramitā | Ayuhyanā | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Kākana | Svāhā | Muktikāte | Sarvabhaviśuddhi | Mahānaya | Parivari | Svāhā || If one were to personally transcribe it...
Teaching others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essential Points of the School of Amitāyus* can eliminate all grave offenses, such as the five sins of immediate retribution.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayu-ghyānāya svapini-sicidhā-rājāya tathāgatāya tadyathā oṃ sarva-saṃskārā pariśuddhe dharmatā gagane svāhā | amoghatīkṛte svabhāva-viśuddhe mahānayā parivare svāhā || If one were to personally transcribe this:
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus*,
and receives, maintains, reads, and recites it, even if they have committed offenses, [they shall be purified].
It is like Mount Sumeru, which can completely eliminate [all obstacles].
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya ayuḥ-vidhānāya supramiṣṭitāya rājāya | Tathāgatāya tadyathā | Oṃ sarvasaṃskārā pariśuddhe dharmatāyāṃ kāṅkṣāṇe svāhā | Mocaka-ti sarvabhava-viśuddhe mahānayapariṇaye svāhā.* If one were to personally transcribe it...
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus*,
and upholds, receives, reads, and recites it,
then whether it be Māra or the retinues of Māra, [they shall be unable to cause harm].
Yakṣas and rākṣasas shall find no opportunity against them,
and they shall never meet with death by violence.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Apāramitā | Ayuhyanā | Supini-siddhata | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Kākana | Svāhā | Muktikā-ti | Sarvabhaviśuddhi | Mahānaya | Parivari | Svāhā || If one were to personally transcribe it...
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essential Points of the Infinite Life*,
and upholds, recites, and reads it,
then at the time of their death, [they shall...]
There were ninety *koṭis* of Buddhas who appeared before that person,
and he received the Buddhas' outstretched hands.
One will be able to travel to all buddha-fields.
Do not give rise to doubt or uncertainty regarding this sutra.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāya supinīścitte rājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | oṃ sarvasaṃskāra pariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | amoghatikṣaye sarvabhaviśuddhe mahānayapariśuddhe svāhā || If one should write this out oneself...
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus*,
and upholds, receives, reads, and recites it,
they will always be protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings who follow them.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Apāramitā | Ayuhyanā | Supini-siddhata | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Kākanā | Svāhā | Mucitakati | Sarvabhaviśuddhi | Mahānaya | Parivari | Svāhā. If one were to personally transcribe it...
If one teaches others to transcribe this *Sūtra on the Essentials of the School of Amitāyus*,
and upholds, receives, reads, and recites it,
they shall attain rebirth in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, the Pure Land of Amitābha.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayur-hetave | Svapnēśvarāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskārā | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Amṛtākarṣiṇi | Sarvabhayaviśodhani | Mahānayā | Parivartaye | Svāhā. If there is any place where one has personally transcribed [this], [there shall be great merit].
Wherever this Sūtra of Immeasurable Life is transcribed, that place shall be treated as a stūpa;
all should pay homage with reverence. This applies even if it is in the hands of an animal.
Or even birds and beasts who hear this sutra—
beings of such kinds as these shall all,
before long, attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayuḥ-hetunā svapnī-siddhaye tathāgatāya tadyathā oṃ sarva-saṃskāra-pariśuddhe dharma-te gagane svāhā | amogha-te sarvārtha-siddhe mahā-naye pari-vare svāhā.* If one personally transcribes this *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, or causes another to transcribe it;
One shall ultimately never again receive a female body.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Apāramitā | Ayuhyanā | Supini-siddhita | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhi | Dharmatā | Kākana | Svāhā | Mocakati | Sarvabhaviśuddhi | Mahānaya | Parivari | Svāhā. If there are those who can bestow even a small portion of this sūtra upon others...
If one were to perform a gift of the seven treasures filling the trichiliocosm,
[the *dhāraṇī* is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāya supinidṛṣṭāya rājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | amoghadṛṣṭe svāhā | bhagavatīśuddhe mahānaye parivare svāhā ||* If there be anyone who is able to make offerings to this sūtra...
This is then no different from making offerings to all the various sūtras.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāntāya | Supinī-siddhaye | Rājāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra-pariśuddhe | Dharmatā-gaganāya | Svāhā | Amoghadhāriṇe | Sarvabhaya-pariśodhani | Mahānāga-parivare | Svāhā || Thus, [it is the same for] Vipaśyin Buddha.
Śikhin Buddha, Viśvabhū Buddha, Krakucchanda Buddha, and Kanakamuni Buddha.
If there is anyone who makes offerings of the seven precious jewels to Kāśyapa Buddha or Śākyamuni Buddha.
The merit of these seven Buddhas is thus limited; however,
to copy and uphold this Sūtra of Immeasurable Life [yields far greater merit].
All merits are immeasurable. The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | oṃ sarvasaṃskārapariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | amoghatīkṣṇe sarvabhayaviśodhani mahānaye parivare svāhā || If there are the seven precious jewels and so forth...
If one were to give Mount Sumeru as a gift,
one might still be able to know the limit of that merit; however, the merit of this *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life* cannot be known by number.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate | Aparimitāya | Ayuhkalpāna | Supini-siddhaye | Rājāya | Tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Sarvasaṃskāra | Pariśuddhe | Dharmatā | Gaganā | Svāhā | Mocayakari | Sarvabhaya-viśodhani | Mahānayā | Parivartaye | Svāhā || Just as the number of drops in the waters of the four great oceans may be known, [so too may the merits of this recitation be known].
The karmic retribution produced by this *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life* is beyond measure.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

Namo bhagavate āparimitāya ayuḥkṣayāya supinīścitte rājāya tathāgatāya tadyathā oṃ sarvasaṃskāra-pariśuddhe dharmate gagane svāhā | Amoghatikṣaye sarvabhaya-vaśīkarī mahānaye parivari svāhā || If one writes this oneself...
They shall cause this Sūtra of Immeasurable Life to be transcribed, and furthermore,
they shall protect, uphold, and make offerings to it.
Just as one respectfully makes offerings to the Tathāgatas in all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions without distinction,
the dhāraṇī is as follows:
Through the power of giving, one can achieve perfect awakening; the Lion among Men awakens to the power of giving.
Through the power of giving, one’s fame can spread everywhere; through the gradual stages of compassion, one is most able to enter [the path].
Through the power of upholding the precepts, one can achieve perfect awakening; the Lion among Men awakens to the power of upholding the precepts.
The power of upholding the precepts causes one’s fame to be heard everywhere; The stages of compassion enable one to enter most effectively.
The power of patience enables the attainment of perfect enlightenment; One who awakens to the power of patience is a lion among men.
The power of patience causes one’s fame to be heard everywhere; The stages of compassion enable one to enter most effectively.
Through the power of diligence, one can achieve perfect awakening; the Lion among Men awakens to the power of diligence.
Through the power of diligence, one’s fame is heard everywhere; through the stages of compassion, one is most able to enter meditative concentration.
Through the power of meditative concentration, one can achieve perfect awakening; the Lion among Men awakens to the power of meditative concentration.
The power of meditative concentration can cause one’s fame to be heard everywhere; The power of compassion can most effectively lead others through its gradual stages.
The power of wisdom can bring about perfect enlightenment; Those who realize the power of wisdom are lions among men.
The power of wisdom can cause one’s fame to be heard everywhere; The power of compassion can most effectively lead others through its gradual stages.
At that time, after the Tathāgata had spoken this sutra,
all those in the world— devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and so forth— [were filled with joy].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
they were all greatly rejoiced;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Tian Guangtan’s Discourse on Broad Discussion
